title: Sell Mineral Rights in Mannington, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Mannington, WV
metaDescription: Mannington, Marion County minerals: Route 250 Marcellus corridor acreage, legacy Big Injun wells, and multi-generation heir title work.
heroLead: Mannington sits directly in Marion County's Route 250 development corridor, where legacy Big Injun wellbores and newer Marcellus units now share the same ground.
intro: As one of the larger towns along Marion County's active drilling corridor, Mannington has seen both continued interest in its legacy shallow production and steady horizontal permitting on surrounding tracts. The two production eras coexist on a lot of acreage here, which makes confirming current lease and royalty status especially worthwhile.

sections.heading: Route 250 corridor development
paragraphs: Horizontal units running through the Mannington area have pooled multiple original farm tracts, and new pad permitting continues periodically as operators extend development along the corridor. If your acreage sits within one of these units, your royalty share is calculated against the unit's total acreage rather than tied to a single well.

sections.heading: Legacy Big Injun wells still on the books
paragraphs: Many Mannington-area tracts also carry older shallow wellbores producing from the Big Injun sand, some still paying under decades-old flat-rate lease terms. These older leases and the newer Marcellus leases on the same or adjacent acreage are usually separate instruments, so it's worth confirming both when reviewing your ownership.

sections.heading: Family ownership split across generations
paragraphs: Mannington's mineral-owning families have often held their acreage for generations, with interests splitting among children and grandchildren at each inheritance. It's common to find a single original tract now divided among a wide group of heirs, several of whom may not be actively tracking their royalty status.

faqs.question: Are Mannington-area Marcellus wells paying more than the legacy Big Injun wells?
faqs.answer: Production volumes and lease terms vary by tract and by which lease governs each well. Comparing your specific division orders is the only reliable way to know what each interest actually pays.

faqs.question: How do I find out if my Mannington tract is in a pooled unit?
faqs.answer: Request the unit plat from the operator or have a courthouse records check run against filed pooling orders at the Marion County Courthouse in Fairmont.

faqs.question: My grandfather's original lease is still on file — is it still valid?
faqs.answer: If the well is still producing and the lease was held by production, it can still be in force decades later. A title check confirms whether it's still active and what terms currently apply.

faqs.question: Can I sell my share without locating every cousin who might also be an heir?
faqs.answer: Yes, we buy individual documented fractional interests directly, without requiring the full family group to participate.
